references.text: Joseph's two dreams about his family bowing down to him. When his brothers now bow before Joseph in Egypt, he remembers these dreams and sees their fulfillment.
The brothers bow with their faces to the ground before Joseph - the direct fulfillment of the dreams that Joseph now recalls.
The first dream where the brothers' sheaves bowed down to Joseph's sheaf, which is now literally fulfilled when the brothers come to buy grain.
Joseph looks back on the whole story and recognizes that what his brothers meant for evil, God turned into good - a reflection on God's plan already hinted at in the dreams.
The psalmist's summary of Joseph's story, from captivity to exaltation, confirming that God's word and plan were fulfilled through Joseph's life.
Direct narrative connection where Joseph recalls the dreams from chapter 37 to interpret his brothers' arrival.
Joseph's claim in 44:15 to have the ability to interpret dreams is the direct theological fulfillment of the dreams mentioned in 42:9.
